request.spec:
A person may name other people on the sheet as their patrons, one at a time from their row (not
themselves, and not the same person twice; a refusal shows an error on the row; PATRON_ADDED
name=<name> patron=<patron name>). Show each person's patrons (names, comma and space separated,
sorted) and their backing: their patrons' due-totals added up, skipping n/a, 0.00 with no
patrons.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A person may name other people on the sheet as their patrons, one at a time from their row (not
themselves, and not the same person twice; a refusal shows an error on the row; PATRON_ADDED
name=<name> patron=<patron name>). Show each person's patrons (names, comma and space separated,
sorted) and their backing: their patrons' due-totals added up, skipping n/a, 0.00 with no
patrons.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
People can now name other people on the sheet as their patrons, and each row shows their patrons and their backing. `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec.

**How it works**
- **Stored data:** a new migration, `V22__patron.sql`, adds a `patron` table. Its primary key is (person, patron), so the database itself also blocks naming the same patron twice.
- **Server:** a new endpoint, `POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/people/{personId}/patrons`, backed by `AddPatron`.
  - It refuses a person who isn't on the sheet, the person themselves, or a patron already named. A refusal writes nothing.
  - On success it writes `PATRON_ADDED sheet=… by=… name=<name> patron=<patron name>` to the audit file.
  - `GET …/people` now also returns the list of patrons alongside the people.
- **Front end:** a new `features/patrons/patrons.slot.tsx` adds these columns to each person's row:
  - `person-patrons`: the names, sorted and joined with ", ".
  - `person-backing`: the patrons' due-totals added up, skipping n/a; 0.00 with no patrons.
  - A dropdown (`person-patron-select`), an add button (`person-patron-add`) and an error message (`person-patron-error`). The error clears when you pick another name or press add again.

**Choices worth knowing about**
- **Dropdown lists everyone, including the person themselves.** I didn't hide the invalid choices; picking one gets refused by the server and shows the error on the row. Hiding them would also pass the test.
- **Patrons are stored by id.** Names and backing are looked up when the sheet is shown, so renaming a patron, or a change to their due-total (such as putting them on hold), shows up straight away.
- **Retired people can still be patrons**, and their due-totals still count towards backing.
- **Due-total code moved.** To reuse the per-person due-total calculation, I moved `useDueTotals` from `rates.slot.tsx` into its own file, `features/rates/useDueTotals.ts`, without changing it.
